source_text: Hanc esse peccati filiam et aliorum peccatorum matrem atque de ea conqueri apostolum Paulum, cum dicit: Scio, quia non habitat in carne mea bonum [n219] ; et: Non quod volo bonum hoc ago, sed quod odio illud facio [n220] , quod semper a catholicis ita expositum est, ut non ad naturae infamiam, sed ad consuetudinis referretur invidiam.
pass_a_gloss: This to be the daughter of sin and the mother of other sins, and that the apostle Paul complains of it when he says: I know that good does not dwell in my flesh; and: Not that good which I will this I do, but that which I hate I do, which has always been so exposed by catholics that it was referred not to the infamy of nature but to the envy of habit.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will

pass_b_english: [You say] it is sin’s daughter and the mother of other sins, and that the apostle Paul complains about it when he says, ‘I know that good does not dwell in my flesh’ (Romans 7:18), and, ‘I do not do the good I want, but do what I hate’ (Romans 7:15). Catholics have always explained this as blaming habit, not defaming nature.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
